chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who sells another man foodstuff in bulk (akrar), but there is not with him what he can complete for him of what he had sold. So he says to him, 'Take from me in place of each qafiz of wheat, two qafiz of barley, until you have fulfilled whatever was deficient from the measure.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not correct, because the origin of the barley is from the wheat, but he should return the dirhams to him by an accounting of whatever was deficient from the measure.'

key_terms.الْأَكْرَار: Bulk or large quantity of goods
key_terms.قَفِيز: A traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods

ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to handle a shortfall in a bulk food sale according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that substituting wheat with barley in a fixed ratio to cover a shortfall is invalid because the fundamental nature (asl) of the two grains differs, potentially introducing hidden defects (gharar) or inequality in value. Instead, the seller must refund the monetary equivalent of the missing quantity, ensuring precise compensation rather than a potentially unequal barter. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on fairness in commercial transactions and the avoidance of ambiguous exchanges.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>

was asked about the man who sells some Kurras (a unit of measurement) of foodstuff to the man, but there did not happen to be with him what he can complete (the order) for him of what he had sold. So he said, ‘Take from me in place of each Qafees (a unit of measurement) of wheat, two Qafeez of barley until it is fulfilled, whatever was deficient from the measurement. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, it is not correct, because the origin of the barley is from the wheat, but he should return the Dirhams back to him by an accounting of whatever was deficient from the measurement’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Once abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who sells foodstuff to another man in quantity of several kur but cannot deliver what he owes, and says to the other party to accept two Qafiz (a certain unit of measurement) of barley for one Qafiz of wheat to compensate for the deficit. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not valid; the origin of barley is from wheat, however, he can return his dirhams proportionate to the degree of deficit.’”
